solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Unprofessional with boy during PE break in school

indicators.note: something happening during PE sits within those two letters, so they surround the rest

parts.note: physical education, the school sports lesson
lay means not of a profession, as in a lay person
Tim is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A school report complaining that a pupil behaved unprofessionally with a boy in a gym class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unprofessional' looks like a comment on behaviour, but it is the sense of lay, as in a lay person without professional training.
explanation.definitionFit: Playtime is the recess period when schoolchildren go outside between lessons.

clue.text: Royals their sister cut?

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter is chopped off the word

parts.note: the sister of royal sons is a princess

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about royal brothers whose sister has been snubbed or trimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last S of PRINCESS. The question mark flags that 'their' points back to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Princes are male members of a royal family, so they are royals.

clue.text: A man hugs another from the New World

indicators.note: to hug is to hold in one's arms, so the first letters wrap round the other piece

parts.note: taken as written, as the letters AMAN
another man, here Eric, a man's name

explanation.surface: One man embracing another who has arrived from across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hugs' puts ERIC inside A MAN, after its M. 'another' means another man, so any man's name fits.
explanation.definitionFit: The Americas were called the New World by Europeans, so an American is someone from there.

clue.text: Vast liner converted for short breaks

indicators.note: a converted thing is changed into another form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge ocean liner refitted to offer brief holidays at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' rearranges the letters of VAST LINER.
explanation.definitionFit: Intervals are pauses, such as the breaks between acts of a play.

clue.text: Expensive losing diamonds in some corn

indicators.note: losing something means it goes missing, so a letter drops out of the word

parts.note: dear means costly
D is the card-suit abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A costly crop that has had its diamonds taken away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes the D of DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is the seed-bearing head of a cereal plant, so it is part of a corn crop.

clue.text: Place for swimming game

definitions.meaning: a cue sport similar to billiards played on a table with pockets

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a swimming bath and a pocket-billiards game.

clue.text: Deposit metal coating on gold table

parts.note: to plate is to cover with a thin layer of metal
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: An instruction to electroplate a table with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'table' is not furniture here but tableland.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a high flat area of land, also called a tableland or table.

clue.text: Oxygen exercises used on speed run

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
PE, physical education, is school exercise
rate means pace or speed

explanation.surface: A training note: breathing oxygen during workouts to improve running pace.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'used on' just places O and PE above RATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a machine or business is to operate it, a synonym.

clue.text: I assembled returned article

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so this word is written in reverse

parts.note: people who assembled met together

explanation.surface: Someone describes putting together an item that was sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembled' reads like putting something together, but here it means people gathered, met.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or object, which is one meaning of article.

clue.text: Menace near the front of tent, moving

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
moving letters about shifts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Something menacing moves about near the entrance to a tent at a campsite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front of' takes the T of 'tent'; 'moving' rearranges it with NEAR THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Menace as a verb means to intimidate with a show of danger, a synonym.

clue.text: Standards for judging writer sacrificing wife taken in by spies

indicators.note: being taken in by something places you inside it, so these letters go within the spies

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency

indicators.note: sacrificing something gives it up, so that letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spy thriller: an author gives up his spouse after being duped by agents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in by' reads as fooled, but it places the shortened writer inside the spies.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the principles or tests by which something is assessed.

clue.text: A quiet soldier needs time with American kit

parts.note: P is piano, the musical term for quiet
a para is a paratrooper
US, the United States

explanation.surface: A silent soldier needs time and an American to sort out his equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the equipment or gear for a task, just as kit is.

clue.text: Suitable small apartment

definitions.meaning: the short form of the word apartment, as in estate-agent listings

explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for fitting and the standard short form of a flat.

clue.text: Expecting ruling after pressure

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece comes after, below, the first

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure
regnant means reigning, as in a queen regnant

explanation.surface: Someone anticipating a court ruling after being pressured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts REGNANT below P.
explanation.definitionFit: Expecting is the everyday idiom for being with child.

clue.text: Lines held by last Anzacs

indicators.note: letters held by these words are contained within them, running across the two

explanation.surface: A defensive line held by the final Australian and New Zealand troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' finds the letters inside 'last Anzacs'. ANZACs were Australian and New Zealand soldiers of the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: A stanza is a group of lines forming a verse of a poem.

clue.text: Strong wind ripped advert off, initially

parts.note: ripped means torn
an ad is an advertisement

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A gale tore a poster off a billboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the O of 'off'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tornado is a violent rotating storm, the fiercest kind of wind.

clue.text: Pointers being almost not necessary

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: needless means unnecessary

explanation.surface: A remark that giving hints is hardly needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the final S of NEEDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Needles on dials and compasses point at readings, so they are pointers.

clue.text: After start of printing, our editor's served tea?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: At a newspaper, once the presses roll, the editor hands round the tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' takes the P of 'printing'. The question mark marks tea as just one example of what gets poured.
explanation.definitionFit: Pouring is what one does when serving tea from a pot, so served tea is an example.

clue.text: Row after doctor's introducing iodine that's more contaminated

indicators.note: in a down clue the row comes after, below, the doctor
introducing something brings it in, so the letter goes within the doctor

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor
I is the chemical symbol for iodine
a tier is a row of seats

explanation.surface: A quarrel after a doctor applies iodine to something increasingly unclean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but means a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: Dirtier is the comparative of dirty, meaning more soiled or polluted.

clue.text: Part of colonel's unit

indicators.note: part of a word is a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A section of an army colonel's command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' finds the letters inside 'colonel's'.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the unit in counting, the single whole number.

clue.text: Visitor called cutting rest, unfortunately

indicators.note: cutting into something splits it open, so this piece goes inside the other
things gone wrong are out of order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: rang means telephoned

explanation.surface: A caller phoned and broke into someone's sleep, sadly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' turns REST into STER; 'cutting' puts RANG into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranger can be a newcomer or outsider in a place, a visitor.

clue.text: Dawn's daughter — certainly not heavy

parts.note: ay is an old word for yes, certainly
light means not heavy

explanation.surface: A woman called Dawn has a slim daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Dawn looks like a woman's name, but it is the definition, and the 's is just 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn is when daylight first appears, so the two are used for the same thing.

clue.text: Precious metal's left out. Mercury, perhaps?

indicators.note: out means gone, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: gold is a precious metal

explanation.surface: A chemistry puzzle: if precious metal is excluded, does mercury count?
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the L from GOLD. Mercury seems to be the liquid metal, but here it is the Roman messenger.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercury was the Roman messenger deity, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: Make heavy demands on current vehicle

parts.note: to tax is to strain or burden
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Charging a vehicle drains a lot of electricity.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a car hired with its driver, a type of vehicle.

clue.text: Cry over small employer

indicators.note: over means turned over, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: Crying about a minor manager at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SOB into BOS.
explanation.definitionFit: The boss is the person who employs or manages staff.

clue.text: SAS tried sorting out calamity

indicators.note: sorting things out puts them into a new arrangement, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Special forces attempted to resolve a catastrophe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out' rearranges SAS TRIED. The SAS is the British Army's Special Air Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden catastrophe, a synonym of calamity.
